Prevention: Rotate cotton with maize or onion, but not with melon, cucumber, pumpkin, or tomato as they are also hosts of this aphid.
Do not apply too much nitrogen (less than 80-120kg/ha) as it makes cotton attractive to aphids.
Sow early: mid-April to mid-May for middle
Awash; mid-May to mid-July for lower
July for rain fed areas to escape aphids.
Grow long-flowering plants or crops, such as mustard or broad beans at field edge to enhance beneficial ladybird beetles and parasitoids
Monitoring: Check last year’s information about aphid problems in certain cotton varieties in your field or neighbourhood.
Place yellow sticky trap; 1 trap/100 m 2 to check arrival of winged aphids
Look for non-winged or winged tiny pear-shaped soft-bodied aphids (from top leaves down).
Using a hand lens, turn the leaf over and check for aphids twice a week. 1st new leaves of young plants.
Later, examine 5th stem node leaf from top of plant (bloom to boll stage, first open boll to pre- harvest).
Observe presence of honeydew on leaves.
Consider direct control if 5 to 10 aphids per 5th stem node leaf on average per plant and row is reached in period between open boll to pre-harvest.
Direct Control (Non-chemical): Wash aphids off with a water stream/jet from underside leaves during early infestation (2-3 aphids/plant) once a week for 5-15 mins
Manage ants with band of sticky tape around trunk of crop and put sugar soaked sponge at the base of the trunk (1 /50m 2 in small fields) or where ants are seen.
Ants protect aphids from natural enemies.
Prune heavily infested leaves at early stage, and bury.
Mix 100g ground garlic, 10g powder soap, ½ litre water, 2 spoons of oil; after 1 day add 20 litres of water and spray.
Spray animal urine, such as from cows, fermented for 2 weeks, and diluted with water (1:10 or 1:15).
Neem extract max 2 times (2.5-3 litres/ha or 50-60 ml /20 litres water; or 20 – 50g neem seed cake or seed powder / litre water plus few tablespoons of soaps).
Chop 30 to 40 hot peppers into 10 litres warm water (not boiling).
Remove pepper rests, add 10 litres cold water and 20 drops dishwashing soap.
Spray max twice with 1 week interval.
Do not spray at full sunshine
Direct Control (Chemical): When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label.
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year.
